Notation. e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1, DG_i(u)e := (DG_i(u)e_a)_{a ∈ Fin (k+1)}, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α, 𝒟^{k+1} := TestFormOn univ (k+1).

1. IM series. cmcdt_im_series applied to VO, MR and IMC gives the statement IMS: for all P′, k′ and W : ℕ → 𝒟_{k′+1}(ℝ^{P′}) with Σ_i M(W_i) < ∞ there is S such that:
 - HasSum (i ↦ W_i(ω)) (S(ω)) for all ω;
 - M(S) ≤ Σ M(W_i) and spt S ⊆ closure ⋃ spt W_i;
 - S is integer multiplicity if all W_i are.
2. Pieces. For each i choose L_i with G_i L_i-Lipschitz. Apply lipschitz_piece_current to MR, IMC, IMS and to P, k, L_i, G_i, A_i, w_i (A_i is Borel, w_i is measurable and integrable on A_i). This gives an integer multiplicity S_i ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) with S_i(ω) = ∫_{A_i} w_i(u)·ω(G_i u)(DG_i(u)e) du for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}.
3. Mass bound. M(S_i) = S_i.massOn univ = sup{ofReal(S_i(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}, tsupport ω ⊆ univ, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}. Fix such an ω.
 - ofReal(S_i(ω)) ≤ ‖S_i(ω)‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_{A_i} ‖w_i(u)·ω(G_i u)(DG_i(u)e)‖ₑ du (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm; no integrability is needed).
 - For u ∈ A_i, the c-bound with α := ω(G_i u) gives |ω(G_i u)(DG_i(u)e)| ≤ c_i(u)·|ω(G_i u)| ≤ c_i(u), since c_i(u) ≥ 0 and |ω(G_i u)| ≤ 1. So ‖w_i(u)·ω(G_i u)(DG_i(u)e)‖ₑ ≤ ofReal(|w_i(u)|·c_i(u)).
 - The right integrand is measurable, so setLIntegral_mono and sSup_le give M(S_i) ≤ ∫⁻_{A_i} ofReal(|w_i|·c_i).
4. Summability. Σ_i M(S_i) ≤ Σ_i ∫⁻_{A_i} ofReal(|w_i|·c_i) < ∞ (ENNReal.tsum_le_tsum and the hypothesis).
5. Sum. IMS applied to (S_i) gives S with HasSum (i ↦ S_i(ω)) (S(ω)) for all ω. S is integer multiplicity because every S_i is.
6. Identification. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}. Since S_i(ω) = ∫_{A_i} w_i ω(G_i)(DG_i e), the hypothesis and step 5 describe the same real series, with sums T(ω) and S(ω). By uniqueness of sums (HasSum.unique), T(ω) = S(ω). By extensionality (GeometricCurrentOn.ext) T = S, so T is integer multiplicity. ∎

The c-bound gives S_i(ω) ≤ ∫⁻_{A_i}|w_i|c_i for every admissible ω with |ω| ≤ 1, so M(S_i) ≤ ∫⁻_{A_i}|w_i|c_i and Σ M(S_i) < ∞.
IMS gives an IM S with S(ω) = Σ S_i(ω). The hypothesis says T(ω) is the sum of the same series, so T = S by HasSum.unique and extensionality, and T is IM.
